what_happened: The job "Add an audience-check role that rates the live explainer page" failed at admission. The change added an `[audience]` section to athena.toml, but the config schema has no such field, so the file no longer parsed. The change also added an email address to crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs outside the allow-list. athena.toml is a governance file, and the accepted reading did not list it as a deliverable or name it in an acceptance criterion. Admission refused the change and the job ended failed with nothing delivered.
cause: Intake builds the reading without knowing which governance files the outcome will require changing. A new role needs registering in athena.toml, but nothing maps outcomes like "add a role" to protected files or to the config schema. The protection rule and the parse check run only at admission, after the reading is accepted. The mismatch therefore surfaces as a failed job rather than as a corrected reading. Nothing at planning time also warns that a new config section needs a schema change, or that a hard-coded email address breaks the allow-list.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance that scans the planned change for governance-protected paths (athena.toml, workflows, policy files). It would also check that new config keys exist in the schema. When the outcome implies one of these, such as registering a new role, the check would require the reading to list the file as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion, or reject the reading before work starts. The same check should flag any hard-coded address that is not on the allow-list and require it to come from configuration instead.
proposed_request: Add an audience-check role that rates the live explainer page. Registering the role will need changes to athena.toml, which is a governance file. List athena.toml as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion. Use only sections and fields the existing config schema accepts, or extend the schema in the same change so athena.toml still parses. Do not add any email address to crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs. Acceptance: athena.toml parses, the role is registered, and a run of the role against the live page returns a rating.
